chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who arrives from a journey after the afternoon prayer in the month of Ramadan, and he has intercourse with his wife when she has become pure from menstruation. He said: There is no harm in it, so it does not contradict what we mentioned, because we did not command him to abstain as an obligation or necessity, but rather we mentioned it as encouragement and recommendation. And we have clarified in what preceded that it is not permissible for one who breaks his fast in Ramadan for an excuse to have intercourse with his family, unless he fears on himself committing the indecent act and entering into the forbidden, for then it is permissible, and the state is as we described.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.يُوَاقِعُهَا: to have sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a traveler to have intercourse with his wife after returning in Ramadan if she is pure from menstruation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Ishtibār*, clarifying that the prohibition on intercourse for a traveler returning after Asr in Ramadan is a recommended precaution (ta'dib) rather than a strict obligation (ijab), provided one does not fear falling into greater sin. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle of differentiating between mandatory abstention and voluntary restraint based on individual circumstances, reinforcing the flexibility within Ramadan's fasting laws.
